question: To whom did Jesus make his first post-resurrection appearance?
summary: Matthew 28:9 says the first appearance was to the two Marys together. Mark 16:9 and John 20:14-17 say it was Mary Magdalene alone. Luke 24:13-31 has the first identified appearance happen to Cleopas and an unnamed companion on the road to Emmaus. Paul, writing the earliest of these texts, names Cephas (Peter) as the first witness in 1 Corinthians 15:5 and never mentions any of the women at all.

reconcile.connective: Gill reads Paul's Cephas-first list not as contradicting the Gospels but as silently omitting the women's testimony, since Mary Magdalene was actually first.

discrepancy.connective: Bart Ehrman presses the deeper problem: Paul, our earliest witness, names Cephas first and never mentions the women at all.

skeptic.name: Bart D. Ehrman
skeptic.work: Jesus, Interrupted: Revealing the Hidden Contradictions in the Bible (And Why We Don't Know About Them)

pd_work.resource: John Haley, An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874)
pd_work.author: John Haley
pd_work.note: Haley's entry 'Christ's resurrection -- certain narratives; different account of it' (pp. 327-330) works Matthew, Mark, Luke and John into one composite sequence, and his adjacent entry 'Appearances of Christ -- one number; different numbers' (p. 385, citing John 20-21, Luke 24, and 1 Cor 15:5-8) extends the same selective-reporting principle to Paul's list, arguing no evangelist (or Paul) claims to record every appearance.

excerpts.attribution: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63)
excerpts.excerpt_text: Not that he was the first person by whom Christ was seen after his resurrection, for he first appeared to Mary Magdalene, Mar 16:9 but the testimony of the women the apostle omits, and it seems as if Peter was the first of the men that saw Christ when risen, see Luk 24:34.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly reconciles Paul's Cephas-first list in 1 Cor 15:5 with Mark 16:9/Matthew 28:9's claim that Mary Magdalene (and the women) were first, by arguing Paul deliberately omits female testimony rather than denying it happened.
